concept.name: Yield spread
concept.definition: The difference between two yields, typically expressed in basis points. Depending on context it may compare maturities on the same curve (term spread, e.g. 10-year minus 2-year Treasury), or securities of different credit quality at the same maturity (credit spread).
concept.intuition: It is the extra (or lesser) yield one instrument offers relative to another, summarizing how the market prices the difference in time, risk, or liquidity between them.
concept.mechanics: Computed as a simple subtraction of yields at matched or specified maturities; e.g. FRED's T10Y2Y is the 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield minus the 2-year, and term or credit spreads widen or narrow as relative yields move.
concept.formula: s = y_A − y_B, quoted in basis points (1 bp = 0.01 percentage point).
concept.failure_modes: A raw yield spread ignores differences in maturity, coupon, embedded options, and compounding conventions, so comparing spreads across unlike instruments can mislead; spreads also mix risk, liquidity, and tax effects.
concept.misconceptions: A wider spread does not automatically mean a bond is 'cheap'; it may simply reflect genuinely higher expected losses or worse liquidity.
concept.example: If a 10-year corporate bond yields 5.6% and the 10-year Treasury yields 4.3%, the yield spread is 130 basis points.

citations.source: FRED, 10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Minus 2-Year Treasury Constant Maturity [T10Y2Y]
